introduction.text: The Chiesa di Nostra Signora di Guadalupe a Monte Mario is a Roman Catholic parish church in Rome’s Monte Mario district, notable for its dedication to the Mexican patron Our Lady of Guadalupe and its status as a titular church of the Catholic hierarchy.

history.description: Construction of the church by the Daughters of Mary Immaculate of Guadalupe, completed between 1928 and 1932.
Establishment of the parish on 22 June 1936 by decree of Cardinal Vicar Francesco Marchetti Selvaggiani Dominici Gregis.
Creation of the titular church title by Pope Paul VI on 29 April 1969.
Appointment of Timothy M. Dolan as cardinal-protector in 2012.

design.description: The presbytery features an altar made of perforated white marble.

art.description: High altar houses the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe, a Mexican priest’s work donated to Pope Leo XIII in 1880 and later to the nuns in 1929.
In 1955, Pius XII proclaimed Our Lady of Guadalupe Queen of labor and a crown made by Guido Veroi was placed on the image.
